nodes.label: notebooks/iTransformer.ipynb
nodes.rationale: The primary deliverable of this repository (CLAUDE.md section 15): a self-contained notebook carrying the whole of src/itransformer_btc/ as definition cells plus orchestration cells that exist in no module. src/itransformer_btc/ is its tested projection, not the other way round. Definition cells are byte-exact slices of their module (D63, guarded by tests/test_notebook_sync.py), which is why docs/NOTEBOOK_MAP.md names the projected module instead of repeating its code. 370 cells (163 code, 207 markdown), 25 phases, 18 producing steps, 18 modules in 144 definition cells.

nodes.label: 0 · Persiapan
nodes.rationale: Find the immutable artifact by glob, never by Dataset slug. Install only what the Kaggle image lacks.

nodes.label: 1 · Pustaka
nodes.rationale: Every import the package uses, loaded once in one place — the Library cell (D66/D67); it is the only cell that imports and the only one carrying `from __future__ import annotations`.

nodes.label: 2 · Konfigurasi & permukaan paket
nodes.rationale: Every protocol number CLAUDE.md section 8.1 locks, as a named constant, then the package's exported names.

nodes.label: 3 · Muat data & hukum segmen
nodes.rationale: Load the immutable artifact, cut the series at every gap, then assert the per-origin window budget by exact equality.

nodes.label: 4 · Pra-proses — dua belas variat
nodes.rationale: Per-bar functions of the current bar, except r which uses the current and previous close. No rolling window anywhere.

nodes.label: 5 · Uji efisiensi pasar
nodes.rationale: ADF, Lo-MacKinlay variance ratio and the Hurst exponent — full sample and each 21-month training sub-block.

nodes.label: 6 · Split walk-forward & scaler
nodes.rationale: H-step purge at both boundaries, and a StandardScaler fitted only on the 21-month training sub-block.

nodes.label: 7 · Dimensionalitas efektif — Stage 3b
nodes.rationale: K_eff is RQ1's independent variable and it is measured before a single epoch runs.

nodes.label: 8 · Algoritma — arsitektur iTransformer
nodes.rationale: Encoder-only. Each variate is one token and attention runs across variates, not across time.

nodes.label: 9 · Loop latih & kontrak keterlacakan
nodes.rationale: GPU-resident training loop with no DataLoader, plus the CLAUDE.md section 12 traceability contract every run writes.

nodes.label: 10 · Metrik & uji statistik
nodes.rationale: Every estimator the paper uses: metrics, DM/Clark-West, survival, and the wild cluster bootstrap for beta1.

nodes.label: 11 · Baseline
nodes.rationale: Ridge, DLinear, PatchTST, LSTM and the two naive comparators — each with an explicit K (D40).

nodes.label: 12 · Perbandingan model
nodes.rationale: Pair matrix, Romano-Wolf stepdown, and the Model Confidence Set (D35).

nodes.label: 13 · Evaluasi ekonomi
nodes.rationale: 00:00 UTC phase, non-overlapping, per segment, DSR per origin (CLAUDE.md section 13.5).

nodes.label: 14 · Peta attention
nodes.rationale: Per-volatility-tercile maps for Figure 5. Calm and stress are data-determined, not chosen after seeing the maps.

nodes.label: 15 · Manifes & eksekutor grid
nodes.rationale: The 1,620-run manifest, resume discovery by glob, the session budget guard, and the two-GPU executor (D68).

nodes.label: 16 · Pelaporan
nodes.rationale: Nine tables and six figures, all rendered from paper_numbers.json — never transcribed by hand.

nodes.label: 17 · Provenance kode & input
nodes.rationale: Every definition cell has run; now record what code was just defined, before anything expensive runs.

nodes.label: 18 · Invarian pra-terbang — Stage 4
nodes.rationale: Three checks that must pass before the grid. All three failed the first time they ran.

nodes.label: 19 · Gerbang Stage 5 — validasi saja
nodes.rationale: Origin 1, 4 K x 3 seeds, scored on the validation sub-block. The test blocks stay shut (D27).

nodes.label: 20 · Grid
nodes.rationale: The full manifest runs in this kernel. Automatic resume, budget guard checked at run boundaries.

nodes.label: 21 · Evaluasi — RQ1, RQ2, RQ3
nodes.rationale: Every number below resolves to a persisted prediction file and one config hash, or it does not enter the manuscript.

nodes.label: 22 · Simpan angka
nodes.rationale: Every table and figure is generated FROM paper_numbers.json, never transcribed.

nodes.label: 23 · Tabel & figure
nodes.rationale: Everything CLAUDE.md section 13.4 promises, rendered from paper_numbers.json.

nodes.label: 24 · Sinkron balik ke src/ — nonaktif
nodes.rationale: The notebook is where you type; src/ is the tested projection. This cell closes the return leg and is fully commented out.

nodes.label: Repository map and the notebook-carries-the-package rule
nodes.rationale: USAGE section 2. The notebook carries the package (D54, D58): definition cells create each module in the kernel namespace, so a Kaggle session needs the notebook and BTCUSDT_1h.parquet and nothing else. Hand-editing a package cell is a defect; the next generator run reverts it silently. tools/build_notebook.py sits outside the package on purpose — it is build tooling, and nothing under src/ may import it.

nodes.label: config.py guarantee
nodes.rationale: Responsibility: Design constants; the derived 15-origin grid; FalsificationOrigin. Key guarantee it enforces: The grid is derived, never transcribed — a stale integer cannot survive a spacing change.

nodes.label: segments.py guarantee
nodes.rationale: Responsibility: Loads the artifact; the segment law; break measurement. Key guarantee it enforces: Raises if the frame reaches outside the half-open data window (D33).

nodes.label: windows.py guarantee
nodes.rationale: Responsibility: Timestamp-validated window enumeration. Key guarantee it enforces: Raises on any window failing t[s+L+H-1] - t[s] == (L+H-1) hours — the defence against positional-index drift.

nodes.label: budget.py guarantee
nodes.rationale: Responsibility: Per-origin/per-block window accounting. Key guarantee it enforces: CLAUDE.md section 11's exact-equality assertion target; asserted against the pooled 4.9% it fires spuriously at fourteen of fifteen origins.

nodes.label: features.py guarantee
nodes.rationale: Responsibility: The twelve variates, per bar, in ladder order. Key guarantee it enforces: Raises on any non-finite variate — impossible unless the segment law did not run. Column order IS ladder order, so rung K is exactly the first K columns and r is channel 0 at every rung.

nodes.label: splits.py guarantee
nodes.rationale: Responsibility: Window semantics per split; the scaler; the tensors. Key guarantee it enforces: Raises if a training target reaches into validation (D24). Two window semantics differing by exactly 119 windows: 'contained' for train/validation, 'origin' for test blocks (D51b).

nodes.label: model.py guarantee
nodes.rationale: Responsibility: Encoder-only iTransformer plus the uniform-attention arm. Key guarantee it enforces: Returns the target channel alone, so the loss is single-channel by construction (D39).

nodes.label: train.py guarantee
nodes.rationale: Responsibility: Training loop; run identity; the two artifacts. Key guarantee it enforces: GPU-resident, no DataLoader; LR halves every 4 epochs (D47).

nodes.label: keff.py guarantee
nodes.rationale: Responsibility: The pre-model measurement and the Stage 3b gate. Key guarantee it enforces: Every K_eff is computed on a training-only span (D44); the gate additionally uses the pre-first-origin span (D02).

nodes.label: metrics.py guarantee
nodes.rationale: Responsibility: Every metric, test and RQ estimator. Key guarantee it enforces: Ratio metrics come from seed-averaged MSEs, never averaged ratios (D42).

nodes.label: baselines.py guarantee
nodes.rationale: Responsibility: The comparators: ridge, DLinear, PatchTST, LSTM, two naive. Key guarantee it enforces: Writes through train.write_artifacts, never its own schema; D45 window alignment is asserted, not assumed.

nodes.label: runner.py guarantee
nodes.rationale: Responsibility: The manifest; resume; budget guard; execute_parallel across every visible GPU. Key guarantee it enforces: Shards the FULL manifest, then subtracts what is done (D53c) — sharding the pending list races two workers against each other.

nodes.label: Stage 1 — ingest
nodes.rationale: spot_klines_btc.py writes the four immutable artifacts. Re-running changes the vintage and section 12 forbids comparing across vintages. --end is exclusive; clip_to_window() enforces it (D33). Expected: 75,216 expected / 75,094 actual bars, 99.8378% coverage, 27 gap blocks, parquet sha256 8270a84b07c2923b.

nodes.label: Stage 2 — segments and the window budget
nodes.rationale: load_bars + usable_mask + budget_table. 75,094 rows, 75,091 usable; exactly 3 unusable bars and they are the same 3 in all three senses. The assertion is exact equality per origin, never against the pooled 4.9%.

nodes.label: Stage 3 — features
nodes.rationale: build_features(bars): 75,091 usable bars -> 75,062 feature rows, 29 dropped, one per segment because r is computed per segment (D52c).

nodes.label: Stage 3b — effective dimensionality and the gate
nodes.rationale: keff.gate_verdict / keff.keff_table. Measured PR 1.00 / 3.33 / 4.27 / 3.98 against the design's 1 / ~3.5 / ~6.5 / ~7. Gate PR at K=8 is 4.393 < 5.0 so the gate does NOT pass; D48's action is disclosure, not a re-cut. K=12's PR is below K=8's, so the redundancy control is stronger than designed, and corr(K, K_eff) = 0.828 makes RQ1's horse race more identifiable.

nodes.label: Stage 4 — pre-flight invariants
nodes.rationale: Three checks, each of which failed the first time it ran: MSE(c*x)/c^2 == MSE(x) (the source spec's form cannot pass); single-batch overfit at dropout=0.0 (~1e-10, versus a 7e-2 floor with dropout on, D52d); Naive-RW mapped as y_z = -mu_g/sigma_g, not 0 (D31).

nodes.label: Stage 5 — the pilot gate, on validation
nodes.rationale: runner.stage5_pilot: 12 runs, origin 1, 4 K x 3 seeds, judged on the validation sub-block never on test (D27). The statistic is Clark-West, not Diebold-Mariano, because the pair is nested (D29).

nodes.label: Stage 6 — the grid
nodes.rationale: Arms with their tags: main itr_ 300, uniform itru_ 75, fresh itrf_ 15, horizon itr_ 144 (48 shared run_ids deduplicated, D53e), ridge rdg_ 60, dlinear dlin_ 45, patchtst ptst_ 45. Two GPUs are two workers; in the notebook they are two threads (D68). nn.DataParallel and DDP both rejected — parallelism belongs at the run level. No Dataset, no DataLoader, no workers.

nodes.label: Stage 7 — evaluation
nodes.rationale: gather_grid -> seed_average, then per RQ: RQ1 tost_equivalence + j_test; RQ2 amplification + panel_beta1; RQ3 decay + b_star + kaplan_meier. Four traps handled: order of operations (seed-averaged MSEs first), the error bar bound to aggregation level (D30), beta1's effective n is the cluster count G = 15 with effective independence near 4 (D28), and a restricted studentized one-sided bootstrap at B = 99,999 whose p-value floors at 1/(B+1) (D53d).

nodes.label: Stage 8 — save
nodes.rationale: artifacts/paper_numbers.json plus five parquet tables. Every table and figure in the manuscript is generated from that file, never transcribed.

nodes.label: `python -m pytest tests/ -q`
nodes.rationale: One command to check the repo is sound — 59 passed, ~13 s, CPU only. USAGE section 9: run the tests first; they found D51, D52 and D53.

nodes.label: `python tools/build_notebook.py`
nodes.rationale: One command after editing src/ — the notebook carries the package (D54). Then pytest tests/test_notebook_sync.py, then commit src/ and the notebook together.

nodes.label: `python tools/notebook_to_src.py`
nodes.rationale: One command after editing a notebook cell: save the notebook first, then run this — the return leg, verified byte-exact (D88). It reads the file on disk, not the live kernel.

nodes.label: `python tools/build_notebook.py --preserve-outputs <exported.ipynb>`
nodes.rationale: Keeping a Kaggle run's outputs: carried onto byte-identical cells only (D86). Never commit the Kaggle export over the generated notebook (D61).

nodes.label: `python -m itransformer_btc.runner --shard 0 --shards 1`
nodes.rationale: One command to run experiments. Flags: --shard/--shards (round-robin BY GROUP so a cell's seeds share one tensor build), --arms, --parquet, --out, --budget-h/--reserve-h checked at run boundaries.

nodes.label: `python tools/build_report.py`
nodes.rationale: Writes paper/{paper_numbers.json,tables,figures,panels}. CPU only, ~4 minutes at the full bootstrap; --check is the drift guard; --bootstrap-b 199 for a fast pass.

nodes.label: run_id = {model}_o{origin}_K{K}_H{H}_s{seed}
nodes.rationale: e.g. itr_o07_K08_H024_s42, itru_o01_K08_H024_s43, itrf_o01_K08_H024_s42. Deterministic and human-readable; changing any component deliberately ORPHANS prior outputs rather than silently reusing a mismatched result.

nodes.label: artifacts/preds/{run_id}.parquet schema
nodes.rationale: block Int8 (1-6; the falsification arm carries 4,5,6 as labels not positions), step Int16 (1..H), timestamp Int64 epoch ms UTC of the WINDOW START (the first target hour is start + L), y_true and y_pred Float32 standardised log-returns. Because L = 96 is a multiple of 24, hour-of-day is preserved, which is what makes the 00:00 UTC non-overlapping phase selectable by timestamp // 3.6e6 % 24 == 0 (D46).

nodes.label: artifacts/meta/{run_id}.json schema
nodes.rationale: Resolved config plus git_sha, code_sha256, input_parquet, input_sha256, input_sha256_source, origin, origin_index, block_labels, k, variates, n_train, n_val, n_test_per_block, mu_g, sigma_g, mu_over_sigma, naive_rw_z, epochs_run, best_val_mse, train_loss, wall_time_s, n_parameters, device, status. git_sha is 'unknown' on Kaggle, so code_sha256 is what identifies the code section 12 requires every number to resolve to (D54b).

nodes.label: Expected numbers — telling a break from a change
nodes.rationale: 75,094 bars / 75,091 usable / 3 unusable; 75,062 feature rows; 15 origins 2020-01..2025-11 at 5-month spacing; 13,545..15,217 training windows on the feature frame (the assertion target); largest training tensor 70.12 MB; 280,472 parameters identical at every rung; 0% test-block loss at 74 of 90 cells, worst 439/720; gate PR at K=8 = 4.393; first measured run itr_o01_K08_H024_s42 at RelMSE 1.0183, R2_oos -0.0183. That last row is worth watching: D20 anticipated +0.004.

nodes.label: Running on Kaggle — Save & Run All, never the editor
nodes.rationale: Attach the data Dataset only, Accelerator GPU T4 x2, then Save Version -> Save & Run All. Discovery is by globbing, never by dataset slug. Do NOT attach the repository and do not add src/ to sys.path — the notebook asserts 'itransformer_btc' not in sys.modules and fails loudly, because an on-path copy shadowing the definition cells would make every number traceable to code that is not in the cells above. Never the interactive editor: the 20-minute idle timeout kills long sessions and hitting the 12 h wall interactively loses /kaggle/working entirely.

nodes.label: Session chaining and mid-grid resume
nodes.rationale: Session N writes to /kaggle/working; Save Version publishes it as a Dataset; session N+1 attaches it as input. At most ONE run is lost (~30 s) because an interrupted run leaves no meta. pending() = manifest - completed matched by run_id, roots discovered by glob over /kaggle/input/*/preds and /kaggle/input/*/*/preds. Two guards: evaluation cells gated on GRID_COMPLETE (D54e) because a half-panel beta1 is a different estimand not a noisier one, and the budget guard bounds the SESSION not the worker (D54f).

nodes.label: Troubleshooting table — symptom to cause
nodes.rationale: Nine named failures with their causes, ending in the rule that carries the rest: a result that looks too good is LEAKAGE until proven otherwise. 'ValueError: the purge did not hold' is a real leak and the assertion must not be loosened; 'unbalanced panel' means finish the grid, because beta1's within-slope identity needs balance.

nodes.label: Tashman (2000), Out-of-sample tests of forecasting accuracy
nodes.rationale: READ (14 pp), journal PDF on disk. THE canonical citation for rolling-origin evaluation. Section 3.1 names the three defects of a fixed origin; 4.3 the calendar argument; 4.4 states this study's rolling-window rationale verbatim in 2000 ('the comparison would be confounded if the second fit period were longer than the first'); 4.2 raises the recalibration objection; 6.2.1 grounds RelMSE by telling forecasters to avoid scale-dependent measures and use a ratio against a naive method. He does NOT establish that rolling-origin errors are statistically dependent — citing him for that would be citing what he did not write.

nodes.label: Bergmeir & Benitez (2012), On the use of cross-validation for time series predictor evaluation
nodes.rationale: Rolling-origin captures performance across differing conditions.

nodes.label: Hyndman & Athanasopoulos (2021), Forecasting: Principles and Practice
nodes.rationale: Section 5.10 — the textbook statement of time series cross-validation on rolling origins.

nodes.label: Giacomini & White (2006), Tests of conditional predictive ability
nodes.rationale: The econometric ground for a FIXED rolling window: their framework treats a forecast as the output of a method estimated on a finite, non-growing window, so estimation error does not vanish; an expanding window sits outside it.

nodes.label: Pesaran & Timmermann (2007), Selection of estimation window in the presence of breaks
nodes.rationale: Under structural breaks the optimal window is finite.

nodes.label: Rossi (2013), Advances in forecasting under instability
nodes.rationale: Out-of-sample performance is itself time-varying.

nodes.label: Bergmeir, Hyndman & Koo (2018), A note on the validity of cross-validation for evaluating autoregressive time series prediction
nodes.rationale: READ (18 pp), Monash working-paper copy (the July 2017 preprint, not the CSDA version of record). Cited AGAINST this study, which is the stronger move: Theorem 1 PROVES K-fold CV valid under A1 stationary/ergodic AR(p) in the target's own lags and correctly specified, A2 LOO consistency, A3 errors an MDS. A1 fails twice here (8-12 distinct variates, and stationarity is what RQ2/RQ3 exist to test) and A3 fails by construction at H = 24, where an optimal h-step error is MA(23) — the same fact section 9.2's rectangular truncation lag 23 already asserts. Their own remedy, a Ljung-Box test on pooled OOS residuals, is NOT currently run.

nodes.label: Cerqueira, Torgo & Mozetic (2020), Evaluating time series forecasting models
nodes.rationale: READ (28 pp), arXiv v1 on disk. The empirical half, on half-hourly/hourly/daily data: 11 estimators over 62 real series. On the 31 non-stationary series plain CV falls to among the worst; and the direction of bias is systematic — CV UNDER-estimates the loss while out-of-sample and prequential methods OVER-estimate it. That finding is the one for the manuscript: this study's headline is a null, and an optimistically biased estimator is precisely the one that manufactures skill that is not there.

nodes.label: Lopez de Prado (2018), Advances in Financial Machine Learning
nodes.rationale: Chapter 7 — the source of purging in a financial-ML setting, of the embargo and of CPCV itself.

nodes.label: Kaufman, Rosset & Perlich (2012), Leakage in data mining
nodes.rationale: The general taxonomy: leakage in FEATURES versus leakage in TRAINING EXAMPLES. The purge closes the second class; section 5.3's no-rolling-feature property closes the first, and this vocabulary is what makes 'structurally absent' checkable rather than asserted.

nodes.label: Hansen & Timmermann (2015), Equivalence between out-of-sample forecast comparisons and Wald statistics
nodes.rationale: The sample-split ratio is not innocuous: the power of an out-of-sample comparison depends on where the split falls, so a split chosen after seeing results is a researcher degree of freedom.

nodes.label: Gama et al. (2014), A survey on concept drift adaptation
nodes.rationale: Source of the blind (periodic) versus informed (drift-triggered) retraining distinction that RQ3 maps onto directly, and the nearest published relative of the falsification arm.

nodes.label: Lu et al. (2019), Learning under concept drift: a review
nodes.rationale: The recent review beside gama2014survey.

nodes.label: Zliobaite et al. (2015), Evaluation methods and decision theory for classification of streaming data with temporal dependence
nodes.rationale: Evaluation under temporal dependence is misleading without a persistence-style baseline — which is why section 7 makes Naive-RW mandatory.

nodes.label: Arian, Norouzi Mobarekeh & Seco (2024), Backtest overfitting in the machine learning era
nodes.rationale: READ (27 pp), Knowledge-Based Systems 305. Concludes CPCV BEATS walk-forward, and is answered from its own methods section: its walk-forward is CrossValidatorController('walkforward', n_splits=4) — a single backtest path its own 2.4.7 says 'tests the strategy only once', i.e. Tashman's fixed-origin design deprecated in 2000; its purgedkfold and combinatorialpurged each receive embargo=0.02 while walkforward receives NO purge at all, so the gap confounds combinatorial with purged; and its 2.4.2 endorses walk-forward for MODEL DECAY specifically, 'alongside other methods like CPCV'. Effect sizes: eta^2 = 0.0102 on PBO, 0.4523 vs 0.4005, walk-forward vs K-Fold p = 1.0.

nodes.label: Inoue, Jin & Rossi (2017), Rolling window selection for out-of-sample forecasting with time-varying parameters
nodes.rationale: Window length is a free parameter with real consequences and is estimable. THIS STUDY DOES NOT ESTIMATE IT — cite in Limitations, do not imply the 24 months were optimised.

nodes.label: Arnott, Harvey & Markowitz (2019), A backtesting protocol in the era of machine learning
nodes.rationale: The protocol-level authority for pre-registration, held-out test periods and reporting the full trial count.

nodes.label: Bailey & Lopez de Prado (2014), The deflated Sharpe ratio
nodes.rationale: The trial-count consequence of opening the test period once.

nodes.label: Makridakis, Spiliotis & Assimakopoulos (2018), Statistical and machine learning forecasting methods: concerns and ways forward
nodes.rationale: ML methods underperforming simple statistical benchmarks out of sample, under a rolling-origin protocol, over a large series collection. Read in the frame the protocol establishes, this study's 'no model beats Naive-RW' is a replication, not a bug.

nodes.label: Cameron, Gelbach & Miller (2008), Bootstrap-based improvements for inference with clustered errors
nodes.rationale: Supplies the clustered inference; the asymptotic refinement comes from bootstrapping the t-statistic, not beta-hat.

nodes.label: MacKinnon, Nielsen & Webb (2023), Cluster-robust inference: a guide to empirical practice
nodes.rationale: The companion to cameron2008bootstrap for the wild cluster bootstrap; restricted (WCR) rather than unrestricted, because WCU is severely size-distorted at small G.

nodes.label: Baur, Cahill, Godfrey & Liu (2019), Bitcoin time-of-day, day-of-week and month-of-year effects
nodes.rationale: Supplies the PREMISE for the 5-month spacing, which would otherwise read as numerology: month-of-year, day-of-week and time-of-day effects measured in Bitcoin specifically. The confound is documented in this asset; the spacing is the response to it.

nodes.label: Ma & Tanizaki (2019), The day-of-the-week effect on Bitcoin return and volatility
nodes.rationale: Measures the same calendar-effect class independently of baur2019calendar.

nodes.label: Figure 1 — the walk-forward scheme, two panels
nodes.rationale: report._figure1 draws from config.ORIGINS and nothing else. Upper panel: fifteen rows, one per origin, each carrying a 21-month training sub-block, a 3-month validation sub-block and six 30-day test blocks, with purge markers at both boundaries; the shape itself states that the window is rolling and fixed-length, that origins are 5 months apart, and that consecutive rows overlap by 79.2% of their training data. Lower panel: origin 1 resolved in days, because at the eight-year scale H = 24 h is 0.03% of the training window and thinner than the line drawn for it — the purge bands are drawn WIDER than 24 hours and the title says so.

nodes.label: Element 1 — multiple origins, not one train/test split
nodes.rationale: A single split estimates accuracy at one point in one regime; its error is an estimate with a sample size of one origin. Pack (1990), via Tashman, measured one method's MAPE at lead 4 moving 3.1% -> 5.8% across test periods.

nodes.label: Element 2 — chronological ordering preserved; no K-fold, no shuffling
nodes.rationale: RQ2's independent variable is time since training. Any scheme that reorders blocks leaves it undefined.

nodes.label: Element 3 — rolling 24-month window, not expanding
nodes.rationale: With an expanding window the training-set size grows with each origin, so model age cannot be separated from training data volume — and RQ2 is a claim about age. Tashman's section 4.4 states this study's exact argument, in 2000.

nodes.label: Element 4 — window length = 24 months
nodes.rationale: A sample-budget choice: 13,545-15,217 training windows on the feature frame against 12 x 96 input dimensions. The window length is a free parameter this study FIXES rather than estimates, and Limitations must say so.

nodes.label: Element 5 — 21/3 train-validation split inside the window
nodes.rationale: Early stopping and ridge alpha are selected somewhere, and that somewhere must be inside the training window and before the origin.

nodes.label: Element 6 — H-step purge at BOTH boundaries
nodes.rationale: A training window whose 24-step target reaches past the boundary carries post-boundary observations into training. At the train->validation boundary the contaminated split is the one governing MODEL SELECTION (D24).

nodes.label: Element 7 — no embargo, and why the channel is structurally absent
nodes.rationale: An embargo guards the REVERSE channel: a test-period bar influencing a training-set feature value. No feature here uses a rolling window (section 5.3), so that channel does not exist. The argument is CONDITIONAL on section 5.3 and must be re-derived if any rolling feature is ever added.

nodes.label: Element 8 — six 30-day test blocks, no retraining inside them
nodes.rationale: This is periodic (blind) retraining evaluated at a fixed cadence; RQ3 asks what the cadence should be, which requires observing performance as a function of block index.

nodes.label: Element 9 — out-of-sample is everything right of the origin
nodes.rationale: There is no fourth split. A forecaster at o has seen everything before it and nothing after.

nodes.label: Element 10 — errors clustered by origin, not pooled as 90 independent cells
nodes.rationale: Consecutive origins share 79.2% of their training data (58.3 / 37.5 / 16.7% at strides 2-4), so A(i,b) series are dependent by construction. The dependence argument is THIS STUDY'S OWN, from D28's overlap arithmetic. What Tashman supplies instead is his section 6.3: Fildes et al. (1998) over 263 series found the relative RANKING of methods changed appreciably as the origin varied.

nodes.label: Element 11 — CPCV considered and rejected
nodes.rationale: CPCV reorders blocks non-chronologically, leaving time-since-training undefined, and assumes DGP stability across blocks — the assumption this study tests. Cite the objecting paper and ANSWER it; ignoring it is the reviewable failure.

nodes.label: Element 12 — test period opened once, after the design is frozen
nodes.rationale: The Stage 5 gate that repositioned the title ran on VALIDATION, not on test (D27).

nodes.label: Element 13 — the result: no model beats Naive-RW
nodes.rationale: Read in the frame the protocol establishes, this is a replication, not a bug.

nodes.label: Unlicensed choice 1 — the 5-month origin spacing
nodes.rationale: NO published protocol prescribes it. With origins spaced s months and 30-day blocks the calendar month block b lands on is m0 + s*i + (b-1) mod 12, so the months visited form a coset of size 12/gcd(s,12). At s = 6 each block index visits only two calendar months, so a significant beta1 would be observationally equivalent to a month-of-year effect. Only s coprime to 12 decouples the two; among those, 5 maximises the origin count subject to the data span. Present it as a reasoned choice with a stated consequence, never as borrowed protocol.

nodes.label: Unlicensed choice 2 — the falsification arm (fresh model at o + 90 d)
nodes.rationale: Standard rolling-origin protocols do not carry one. It exists because aged-model decay and calendar difficulty are otherwise observationally equivalent: if the aged-minus-fresh gap is zero while beta1 < 0, then beta1 is calendar, not age. Report it on RelMSE, NEVER on scaler-space MSE (D60i) — the two arms carry different sigma_g.

nodes.label: Unlicensed choice 3 — the six-block, 180-day test span
nodes.rationale: A convention, not an optimum. Its consequence is stated rather than hidden: b* resolves only to 30-day granularity out to 180 days, so 'no decay detected within 180 days' is a RIGHT-CENSORED result and must be worded as one — not the situation that occurred (D60b).

nodes.label: The recalibration objection (Tashman section 4.2), answered in three parts
nodes.rationale: The sharpest objection a referee who has actually read Tashman will raise, and it was found by reading him rather than by citing him: 'Updating without recalibrating imposes an arbitrary handicap.' Three things separate the cases and all three belong in the manuscript. (1) His mechanism is a static regression where a new data point changes neither inputs nor coefficients; here the INPUTS move — each of the 720 forecasts per block is issued from a different 96-bar window, only the weights are fixed. (2) The frozen weights ARE the measurement: RQ3 asks what accuracy costs when a model is left in place. (3) Recalibration does happen, every five months at each of the fifteen origins, and the falsification arm is precisely the recalibrated comparator he asks for, run at one interior point. Saying only the third invites the reader to ask why the interior of the test span was left alone.

nodes.label: Why the strongest paper FOR cross-validation does not license it here
nodes.rationale: Section 2.1 exists because 'K-fold CV is fine for time series, Bergmeir proved it' is the single most likely challenge to section 8, and the answer is not a preference but an assumption check that either passes or fails. A1 fails twice (multivariate inputs; stationarity is the thing RQ2/RQ3 test) and A3 fails by construction at H = 24 (MA(23) errors cannot be an MDS) — using K-fold CV would contradict the rectangular variance estimator the same manuscript defends. Scope stated honestly: both papers study univariate, purely autoregressive, one-step-ahead forecasting; they are cited for the assumption boundary and the direction of the bias, not as evidence about this architecture.

nodes.label: Answering arian2024backtest from its own methods section
nodes.rationale: Section 4.2. Three facts about their code, stated FIRST: single path (n_splits=4, their own 2.4.7 calls it 'a single backtest path ... it tests the strategy only once'), unpurged (walkforward receives neither times= nor embargo=0.02 while the CV variants do, so the measured gap confounds combinatorial with purged), and their 2.4.2 endorses walk-forward for MODEL DECAY specifically. The estimand argument — PBO and DSR measure strategy-SELECTION overfitting among candidates competing on one return series — is stated LAST, because leading with it reads as special pleading while the two facts about their code do not. This is Related Work material, not only a defensive paragraph.

nodes.label: What Tashman also settles about the metrics (section 6.2.1)
nodes.rationale: Avoid scale-dependent error measures such as RMSE and MAD when averaging over series that differ in scale or volatility; use a RATIO against a naive method instead, which 'standardizes the component series for degree of change and, hence, degree of forecasting difficulty'. RelMSE = MSE_model / MSE_naive is the squared-error analogue, and that phrase is D05's argument written in 2000. D60i — no cross-origin comparison on scaler-space MSE, because each origin carries its own sigma_g — is the same rule reached the hard way, by a units artefact that made a falsification-arm number read backwards.

nodes.label: Status of the citations — resolved is not read
nodes.rationale: Every DOI was confirmed against Crossref by DOI LOOKUP, not by relevance search (D89 explains why the distinction matters). verified=doi-resolved means the identifier and metadata are right and the source has NOT been read end to end; section 13.3 forbids citing above the tier actually reached. Of 70 bib entries, 8 are read, 53 doi-resolved, 8 artifact, 2 screened, against a 35-45 reference budget — the largest single piece of work left in the project, and no part of it is computational. Reading the four load-bearing entries changed the DOCUMENT rather than only its flags: element 3 gained Tashman's 4.4 sentence, element 10 LOST a claim he does not make, and sections 4.1 and 4.2 exist only because the sources were opened.

nodes.label: Draft paragraph for manuscript section 3.6
nodes.rationale: Section 5 is a ready draft of the walk-forward methodology paragraph with every bibtex key in place, so the manuscript prose and this document's element table cannot drift apart.

nodes.label: Verified state of the working tree at 2026-09-09
nodes.rationale: 1,620 runs, all status complete, under a SINGLE code_sha256 bfb43f21028da322...; every run records one input hash and the actual parquet digest matches 8270a84b07c2923b...; paper/paper_numbers.json already records 1,620 runs and points at the correct grid digest, so the older claim that the report lagged at 894 runs does NOT hold for the current report artifact; test suite 229 passed in 308.77 s. No grid retraining was done for this audit — the lookback re-comparison used stored predictions. A01-A15 are audit finding ids, not divergence-register ids.

nodes.label: A01 — evaluation time shifts by the lookback, so L comparisons do not use the same target hours
nodes.rationale: CRITICAL, verified on actual predictions. splits.window_starts(..., semantics='origin') picks ts[first] inside the test block and _gather() then takes targets from first + seq_len, while train.py stores split.ts as `timestamp` — which is the INPUT START. At origin 1, seed 42, K=8, H=24 all three arms store 2020-01-01 00:00 UTC while the first actually-scored target bar is 2020-01-03 (L=48), 2020-01-05 (L=96) and 2020-01-09 (L=192). Equal origin/block labels therefore do not guarantee equal targets. This is NOT evidence that training read test labels — inputs still precede targets; the defect is the time contract and the equality of the evaluated sample. On a fair intersection over 15 origins and 5 seeds, mean delta-RelMSE L192-L96 = -0.004164 (all 15 origins favour L192) against the previously reported -0.003506, so the direction survives but the magnitude and comparison basis must be restated. Missing: an explicit contract for input_start, forecast_origin and target_timestamp, plus an assertion that a model pair scores the same actual targets.

nodes.label: A02 — matched-K does not isolate K_eff
nodes.rationale: HIGH, design weakness visible from the configuration. features.py and D70 say PR is the only thing that moves between the two K=8 subsets, but `redundant` carries all three volatility estimators plus log_mean_trade_size while `orthogonal` substitutes upper_shadow, lower_shadow and vwap_location — so INFORMATION CONTENT moves with PR. An orthogonal win could come from more target-relevant features, an easier representation, instance normalisation, or reduced redundancy; the two subsets do not separate those. 'orthogonal' also does not mean the feature vectors are mathematically orthogonal, and PR is a correlation-spectrum measure, not a measure of predictive information about future returns. Claimable now: the subset with this composition and higher PR has lower error in the tested configuration. Not claimable: that raising K_eff CAUSES accuracy.

nodes.label: A03 — the RQ1 J-test does not apply the clustering the methodology declares
nodes.rationale: CRITICAL for RQ1's inferential claim, verified. metrics.j_test demeans by origin x block but its covariance is sigma2 * pinv(X.T @ X) — conventional OLS. Fixed effects do NOT automatically produce clustered standard errors. Recomputed with a CR1 covariance clustered by origin and t(14): K augmented by fitted K_eff p 0.001123 -> 0.006249; K_eff augmented by fitted K p 0.728132 -> 0.429679. The 5% decision does not flip; the finding is that the reported p-value is not the p-value of the promised procedure. The CR1 diagnostic itself does not resolve BETWEEN-origin dependence, and 'about four independent training sets' is an overlap heuristic, not a formal effective-sample-size estimate.

nodes.label: A04 — the nested assumption for Clark-West does not follow from feature subsetting; Naive-RW is structurally problematic under instance normalisation
nodes.rationale: CRITICAL, mathematical analysis plus an implementation counterexample. comparisons.nesting_order classes Naive-RW versus every model, and some K pairs, as nested — but nested INFORMATION SETS are not nested PARAMETRIC MODELS: K=1 -> K=8 changes the token count and the attention operation, so the small model must be shown to be a parameter restriction of the large one. More fundamentally, at K=1 the normalise/denormalise pair gives f(x + c) = f(x) + c, which a constant zero forecast does not satisfy (numeric check at c = 0.2 deviates by ~2.83e-7), so Naive-RW is not automatically a member of the instance-normalised iTransformer function class. Clark-West corrects estimation bias in genuinely nested comparisons; its theory does not transfer to arbitrary neural pairs merely because one has more features. Negative R2_oos remains a valid descriptive measurement.

nodes.label: A05 — the main table, MCS/DM and the pilot compare different statistical objects
nodes.rationale: HIGH, verified. The main table averages MSE ACROSS SEEDS; comparisons.build_panel averages PREDICTIONS across seeds and only then computes loss and MCS — the second is ensemble performance, the first estimates the average single-training model. The identity is mean_seed[(y - pred_s)^2] = (y - mean_seed[pred_s])^2 + var_seed(pred_s). At iTransformer K8 origin 1 the audit measured seed-mean MSE 1.319134 against ensemble MSE 1.310948, a 0.62% gap (0.43% and 0.37% at origins 8 and 15) — material when the effect being read is a fraction of a percent. The pilot is a third object again: stage5_pilot feeds y_val.mean(axis=1) and the H-averaged forecast to Clark-West, testing the CUMULATIVE H-step return error, not the per-step squared error that is the objective. More seeds does not resolve this.

nodes.label: A06 — the MDE attributed to the pilot is computed from test slopes; the pre-registration label needs correcting
nodes.rationale: CRITICAL for reporting credibility, verified on the code path and the number. In tools/build_notebook.py, CODE_RQ2 runs panel_beta1(amp) AFTER the grid is gathered and then minimum_detectable_beta1(beta.within_slopes); amp is the TEST panel. Recomputing from the 15 stored test slopes gives -0.0009202919371959043, exactly the published MDE. Stage 5 uses origin 1 alone, and one origin cannot supply between-15-origin dispersion. So the available number is a post-hoc sensitivity diagnostic, not evidence of prospective power analysis before the test blocks were opened. This does not prove every decision was made after seeing results, but documentation cannot substitute for the provenance and ordering of the measurement. No pre-analysis registry identity or snapshot supporting the 'Pre-Registered' title was found in the repository — evidence may exist outside it. Re-running the grid on already-seen data does not make the analysis prospective.

nodes.label: A07 — the RQ3 decay definition can fire while skill is improving, and does not estimate an optimal cadence
nodes.rationale: CRITICAL conceptually, counterexample verified. metrics.decay uses the mean skill over ALL SIX test blocks as the reference and b_star() then picks the first block worse than that reference by tau — a reference containing the future relative to the early blocks. With per-block skill 1,2,3,4,5,6% (monotone improvement) the mean is 3.5%, so D at block 1 is 71.4% and the code returns b* = 1, event = True at tau = 5%. The estimator detects being below the overall average, not specifically the loss of skill since training. On real results the R2_oos guard excludes every ladder origin, so 'estimand undefined' does match the code's output — the counterexample shows that finding a dataset with positive skill would still not make the definition valid. Separately, a threshold crossing time is not an OPTIMAL cadence: that needs a decision objective, retraining cost and a comparison of policies on the same evaluation calendar.

nodes.label: A08 — RQ2 conflates several senses of model age and is weak for a mechanism claim
nodes.rationale: HIGH, design limitation. Origin 2020-01 has a training cutoff of 2019-10-01 with validation in between, so January weights were selected on gradients from data ending about three months earlier: time since deployment and time since the most recent training observation are two different quantities, and A01's timestamp shift adds another offset. The fresh arm refreshes the training AND validation windows at once, and uses ONE seed per origin while the aged main arm is averaged over five — not automatically a mean bias, but more Monte-Carlo uncertainty on exactly the arm expected to detect a small effect. Origin fixed effects control the average difficulty level per origin; they do not by themselves separate age from within-origin calendar change. A non-significant beta1 supports a descriptive report, not proof that decay does not occur.

nodes.label: A09 — baseline comparison confounds architecture with objective and optimisation budget; the ports differ from the official implementations
nodes.rationale: HIGH, code and metadata verified. iTransformer and LSTM optimise the target return; DLinear and PatchTST use an all-channel loss over engineered features with different distributions and persistence, and early stopping follows each arm's own objective, so the best checkpoint for eight outputs is not the best checkpoint for the return. Budget: DLinear 56/75 and PatchTST 39/75 runs reach the 30-epoch cap against iTransformer's headline 0/300 — reaching the cap does not prove longer training would help, but there is no comparative evidence the ranking is stable after adequate optimisation. Port differences to name: the official iTransformer applies LayerNorm after the whole encoder while the local ITransformer projects the layer-list output with no final encoder norm; the official PatchTST provides BatchNorm and residual attention in its encoder while the local version reuses the iTransformer EncoderLayer. These are experimental adaptations that need explaining, not proof the results are wrong.

nodes.label: A10 — directional accuracy is computed in scaler space, not on the actual return direction
nodes.rationale: HIGH, verified on actual predictions. metrics.directional_accuracy takes the sign of y_true and y_pred directly, but both are stored as z-scores: the sign of (r - mu)/sigma says whether the return is above or below the TRAINING MEAN, not whether the price rose or fell; the relevant inverse is r = z*sigma + mu. At origin 15, iTransformer K8, seed 42, the coded cumulative non-overlapping DA is 44.44% and becomes 47.22% after inverse scaling, and adding the scaler drift back to the cumulative forecast flips 12 of 180 position signs. economics.positions() deliberately uses sum(pred_z)*sigma as a de-meaned forecast while the realised return uses sum(actual_z)*sigma + H*mu — a legitimate strategy if defined that way, but not the same as a strategy on the sign of the raw return forecast. Do not use the word 'raw' for two different transformations.

nodes.label: A11 — the economic evaluation is not yet readable as an executable spot backtest, and Sortino uses the wrong formula
nodes.rationale: HIGH for the economic claim; a tested defect plus design limitations. Positions may be -1: spot data may legitimately be used to simulate long/short, but a short needs inventory/borrowing assumptions and costs this simulator does not carry, so the result must be called a P&L simulation under those assumptions. Gap-spanning windows are excluded on a FUTURE event, which is a scope limitation for conditional forecast evaluation but not available to a trader without an oracle; net_returns() receives only surviving-period positions and no gap calendar, so it cannot charge the close and reopen the narrative implies, and terminal liquidation cost is unmodelled. Sortino has a separate numerical defect: the code takes the standard deviation of negative returns only, whereas downside deviation at MAR = 0 is measured relative to zero with zero contribution above target. On [-1%, -1%, +2%, +2%] the code returns UNDEFINED (two identical losses have zero std) while the correct value under the project's annualisation is 13.5093.

nodes.label: A12 — gap selection bias is not removed by adding a coverage covariate, and the promised training-size control never ran
nodes.rationale: HIGH for generalisation and RQ2, metadata and code verified. Actual main training window counts are 13,545-15,217, ~12.3% spread relative to the minimum; build_origin_tensors() uses all training indices and the manifest carries no arm that equalises them, so the subsampling control section 8.1 and the window budget describe is not an available experimental result. Within an origin the ladder shares the same data across K, so within-origin contrasts are not automatically void; the concern is cross-origin generalisation and the claim that fixed-duration windows remove all sample-size variation. The coverage covariate IS implemented (D80 is not open), but a surviving-proportion covariate does not restore discarded outcomes or prove the missingness is ignorable, and the outage-clusters-on-stress premise needs evidence beyond the gap CSV — a bar absent from a REST artifact does not by itself distinguish maintenance, a trading halt and a data-path loss.

nodes.label: A13 — resume and notebook output preservation can still carry stale vintage forward
nodes.rationale: CRITICAL before any rerun, two verified counterexamples. First, runner.pending filters strictly on the code vintage, but execute() and execute_parallel() call completed_run_ids(roots) again WITHOUT the digest and test is_complete(), which does not compare vintage — so the plan can ask for a rerun the execution then skips. The counterexample, using a temp directory and old code metadata and no model fitting, gives pending=1 -> completed=0, skipped=1, remaining=1. D85 therefore does not close the whole usage path; the current 1,620 runs are still a single consistent vintage by hash. Second, build_notebook.carry_outputs compares the CALLING cell's source but not its dependencies: change f() from returning 1 to returning 2 and the unchanged cell `print(f())` keeps output 1 in the regenerated notebook. Cell-text equality does not prove the output came from the function now defined.

nodes.label: A14 — several methodological justifications are too absolute or do not match what the library does
nodes.rationale: MEDIUM but important for defending the methodology. CLAUDE.md, pyproject.toml and code comments repeatedly claim polars makes center=True unrepresentable, but the official Expr.rolling_mean HAS a `center` parameter with a center=True example: the project's actual protection comes from building per-bar features and checking chronology, not from a library incapacity. Keeping polars is a legitimate decision; the safety reason must be accurate. Likewise an identical parameter count between the uniform-attention and learned-attention arms does not mean identical effective capacity — Q/K are unused on the uniform branch and attention-weight dropout does not run there — so the ablation tests that package of changes, not attention selection in isolation. ARIMA may stay deferred on scope, but ADF and the variance ratio do not PROVE AIC would choose (0,0,0); state that as a conjecture or a pragmatic reason, not an obtained result.

nodes.label: A15 — manuscript, novelty and the boundary of the conclusions are unfinished
nodes.rationale: HIGH for the research deliverable, verified on the documents. paper/manuscript.tex wires up many tables and figures, but abstract, introduction, related work, parts of methodology, limitations and conclusion are still TODO, and the novelty search protocol is empty. README still carries the old comparative title and a 684-run grid; USAGE mixes run and cell counts from several phases; RUN_ANALYSIS keeps historical tables under a note that things have changed. The JSON artifacts are consistent, so the weakness is the READING GUIDE, not grounds to accuse the latest results of stale vintage. 'No out-of-sample skill' must be bounded to the models, target, horizon, preprocessing, sample and aggregation tested: a negative mean R2_oos does not prove no predictability anywhere in Bitcoin or across every attention architecture, and some origins may show positive skill despite a negative average. A 'first' claim needs a checkable literature search log.

nodes.label: Recommended remediation order (six steps)
nodes.rationale: 1. Fix the target-time contract and make the single-run / ensemble / cumulative loss definitions consistent — every later comparison depends on the right object and sample. 2. Correct the nested/non-nested reasoning, the J-test, dependence-aware uncertainty and the provenance of the MDE — this decides what may lawfully be called inferential evidence or pre-specified. 3. Recompute DA and economics on explicit definitions and bound RQ3 to its estimand. 4. Repair the resume path and notebook dependency invalidation with regression checks, so the next rerun really produces and displays a new vintage. 5. Only then weigh baseline sensitivity and feature/sample-size controls AS NEW EXPERIMENTS. 6. Finish the manuscript and the novelty protocol from what is already provable. Not all of this needs a GPU: most metric corrections, aggregation definitions, MDE reporting, some prediction alignment and all the writing can use the artifacts already on disk.

nodes.label: What still stands — the descriptive model ordering
nodes.rationale: From paper/paper_numbers.json main_results.by_model, 15 origins, H=24: Naive-RW 0 (zero forecast on raw return), Ridge K4 -0.000292 (deterministic), LSTM K8 -0.001559 (five seeds), PatchTST K8 -0.016353 (all-channel objective), iTransformer K8 -0.017993 (target-channel objective), DLinear K8 -0.026209. These describe the available evaluation and must be read together with A01-A15; MCS membership and p-values are NOT treated as validated merely because the means reproduce. A negative result against Naive-RW does not make RQ1 meaningless — the error difference between two models that both lose is still researchable; what must be bounded is reading that difference as profitable skill, as a causal K_eff mechanism, or as a trading/retraining recommendation.

nodes.label: External source trail, 9 September 2026
nodes.rationale: Searched in English, focused on primary/authoritative sources tied to each finding: MacKinnon-Nielsen-Webb arXiv 2205.03285 for clustered inference (A03); the Center for Open Science preregistration guidance for existing datasets (A06); Clark & West's 2005 working paper for the CW assumptions (A04); the official thuml/iTransformer and yuqinie98/PatchTST repositories for port fidelity (A09); the CME Sortino note and the Binance Margin introduction for risk metrics and short execution assumptions (A11); and the official polars.Expr.rolling_mean API for the centered-window claim (A14). Snippets were used only as pointers; substantive quotes refer to pages actually opened. No hit counting or systematic screening for novelty was performed.
